claims.text: Current guideline: Surviving Sepsis Campaign international guidelines for sepsis and septic shock, 2026.
claims.quote: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026.

claims.text: Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction from a dysregulated host response to infection. Septic shock: vasopressors needed to keep MAP ≥ 65 mm Hg and lactate > 2 mmol/L despite adequate fluids.
claims.quote: Sepsis is a clinical syndrome of life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. Septic shock is defined as sepsis with persistent hypotension requiring vasopressors to maintain mean arterial pressure ≥ 65 mm Hg and having a serum lactate > 2 mmol/L, despite adequate volume resuscitation.

claims.text: qSOFA: ≥ 2 of respiratory rate ≥ 22, altered mentation, systolic BP ≤ 100 mm Hg calls for further evaluation for sepsis and its source.
claims.quote: Patients with suspected sepsis who have ≥ 2 of the qSOFA criteria should have further evaluation for sepsis and a source of infection. The qSOFA criteria are as follows: Respiratory rate ≥ 22 breaths per minute Altered mentation Systolic blood pressure ≤ 100 mm Hg

claims.text: Outside the ICU, qSOFA predicts inpatient mortality better than SOFA or SIRS.
claims.quote: For patients with a suspected infection who are not in the intensive care unit (ICU), the qSOFA score is a better predictor of inpatient mortality than the SOFA score and SIRS criteria

claims.text: Initial tests: CBC with differential, comprehensive metabolic panel, lactate, blood cultures, urinalysis and urine culture, and cultures from likely sources.
claims.quote: Tests include CBC with differential, comprehensive metabolic panel, lactate, blood cultures, urinalysis and urine culture, and cultures of other body fluids from potential sites of infection suggested by the patient's history, symptoms, and signs.

claims.text: Fluids: 1 L crystalloid rapidly; most patients need at least 30 mL/kg in the first 3 hours.
claims.quote: Initially, 1 L of crystalloid is rapidly infused. Most patients require a minimum of 30 mL/kg in the first 3 hours

claims.text: Still hypotensive: norepinephrine or vasopressin (up to 0.03 units/minute) may be given to raise mean BP to at least 65 mm Hg.
claims.quote: norepinephrine (highly individualized dosing) or vasopressin (up to 0.03 units/minute) may be given to increase mean blood pressure to at least 65 mm Hg.

claims.text: Your notes (Septic Shock row) define sepsis as SIRS + a focus of infection (lactate > 4), severe sepsis as SIRS + multi-system organ failure, and septic shock as sepsis + refractory hypotension.
claims.quote: Sepsis: SIRS + focus of infection (lactate >4) Severe Sepsis: SIRS + multi-system organ failure Septic Shock: sepsis + refractory hypotension
